;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[28 July 2019 Kabul suicide bombing]]
**Gunfire and an explosion kills 20 and injures over 50 in an attack at the [[Kabul]] office of the [[Vice President of Afghanistan|Vice President]]ial candidate [[Amrullah Saleh]], who was slightly injured in the attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-49148761 (BBC News)]
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Libyan Civil War]]
**An [[airstrike]] kills five doctors in a hospital in the southern outskirts of [[Libya]]'s capital [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-49143263 (BBC News)]
*During conflicts in the state of [[Amapá]] in [[northern Brazil]], armed miners invade a [[Indigenous territory (Brazil)|native reserve]] and stab to death an indigenous man. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-49144917 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*At least 42 people die in a [[landslide]] striking a village in [[southern China]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-49143507 (BBC News)]
*Heavy storms across [[central Italy]] kill three people and cause damages. One death was caused by lightning, one by a tornado, and one by getting caught in a flood. [https://www.ilmessaggero.it/italia/maltempo_roma_fiumicino_tromba_d_aria_morta_donna_metro_allagata_ultime_notizie-4645512.html (''Il Messaggero'')]
*The death toll of the heavy floods in [[Nepal]] rise to 113. [https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/floods-landslides-claim-113-lives-in-nepal-1574530-2019-07-28 (''India Today'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Gilroy Garlic Festival shooting]]
**A gunman opens fire at the [[Gilroy Garlic Festival]] in [[Gilroy, California]], killing three people and wounding at least twelve others. The gunman is killed after engaging with the police. Police believe an accomplice is still at large. [https://www.sfchronicle.com/crime/article/Multiple-people-hurt-in-shooting-at-Gilroy-Garlic-14191974.php (''SF Chronicle'')] [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-news/shooting-gilroy-garlic-festival-san-francisco-bay-area-live-updates-today-2019-07-28/ (CBS News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Hong Kong anti-extradition bill protests|Hong Kong protests]]
**Tens of thousands of protesters demanding the resignation of pro-[[China]] [[Chief Executive of Hong Kong]] [[Carrie Lam]] take over the streets in [[Sai Wan]] and [[Causeway Bay]], near China's [[Hong Kong Liaison Office]], despite an official police ban on protests near the Chinese government building. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-china-49143207 (BBC News)]
**During protests, Hong Kong groups organize to put pressure on the [[United Kingdom]], asking for help to uphold the city-state's legal rights. The [[Sino-British Joint Declaration|Joint Agreement of 1997 signed by the UK and China]] outlines that Hong Kong will have legislative and judiciary independence, based on systems implemented there under British rule. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/jul/28/hong-kong-protest-take-democracy-struggle-uk-politicians (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2021 Peruvian general election]]
**[[President of Peru|President]] [[Martín Vizcarra]] announces that he will present a constitutional reform that calls a snap election for April 2020. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-peru-politics/peruvian-president-vizcarra-proposes-early-legislative-elections-idUKKCN1UN0Q0 (Reuters)]

;Sports
*[[2019 Tour de France]]
**In [[Road bicycle racing|road cycling]], [[Colombia]]'s [[Egan Bernal]] wins the Tour de France by 1:11 on general classification over his [[United Kingdom|British]] [[Team Ineos|teammate]] [[Geraint Thomas]]. The 22-year-old Bernal is the first Colombian and first Latin American rider to win the Tour, and the youngest rider to do so since [[1909 Tour de France|1909]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/cycling/49145747 (BBC Sport)]
